title: The Serpent and the Eagle

full_text:
An eagle swooped down from the sky and seized a large serpent in his talons. But the serpent coiled itself around the great bird's body, pinning his wings and coiling around his neck to strangle the monarch of the air.

A country peasant, seeing the eagle's mortal struggle, ran forward and untangled the serpent's coils, freeing the eagle, who soared back into the heavens.

The furious serpent spat venom into the peasant's drinking horn while the man rested under a tree.

As the peasant lifted the horn to his parched lips, the grateful eagle swooped from the clouds, struck the poisoned vessel from the man's hands with his wing, and shattered it upon the rocks, saving his deliverer's life and repaying kindness with loyalty.
moral: An act of kindness shown to the helpless returns as a shield in mortal peril.
